name: training-recipe comparison (memory vs deference to in-context edits)
world: ccgen_t12a3s1_lite (T=12 tasks, A=3 arguments, S=1), seeds 0/1/2
base_data: per task 32 exec + 4 decoy + 2 restatements (494 rows), no policy in context

arms.ctrl: P + 128 ordinary rows (equal amount of data)
arms.M: P with the full original policy in context for each exec/decoy row with probability 0.5
arms.cons: P + 128 consistent rows: same requests as prec's practice rows, original policy in context, label = memory
arms.prec: P + 64 Override practice rows (practised tasks 1-6; 3/4 ask the changed task, 1/4 another task) + 64 Substitute rows (foreign policies of seeds 50/51)

probe_set.override_held: held-out tasks 7-12 edited (vseed 2000+), answer-changing items only
probe_set.substitute: policy of seed 100+s, answer-changing items only

comparison: prec - cons and prec - P on override_held and substitute; seed-stratified item bootstrap 95% CI (10000)

decision_rule_pp.rule: both columns >= 10pp with CI lower bound > 0 -> conflict samples are a method component; both <= 3pp -> analysis only; otherwise add a seed

capability_guard: IFEval (541 prompts) delta vs base; reported per seed, not a non-inferiority proof
